newsItems.headline: UK's FTSE 100 flat as energy gains counter mining losses amid US-Iran flare-up - Reuters
Gold extends decline as Middle East tensions bolster higher-for-longer rate view - Reuters

riskTone.label: BEARISH
riskTone.rationale: US-Iran tensions signal mild risk-off; energy gains offset mining losses keeping FTSE flat, but higher-for-longer rate fears add headwind.

briefing.briefing: Starting with the GBP sign-flip — sterling (GBPUSD) fell -0.39% today, which is normally a tailwind for UK100 because a weaker pound makes the index's big dollar- and euro-earning multinationals (Shell, BP, Unilever, AstraZeneca) worth more in sterling terms — however the model rates this effect as NEUTRAL today, meaning the currency support is being cancelled out by other headwinds. The dominant forces right now are a sharp spike in oil prices (Brent crude +9.71%), which is strongly BULLISH for energy giants Shell and BP — the top-5 index weights — while US equity markets are having a rough session (S&P 500 -0.95%, Nasdaq -2.11%), which typically drags the FTSE lower in sympathy; European markets (DAX -0.39%, EuroStoxx -0.58%) are also pointing softer, and gold is falling -2.92% as rising Middle East tensions (US-Iran flare-up reported by Reuters roughly 4 hours ago) are paradoxically fuelling fears of interest rates staying higher for longer, which hurts growth assets even as it boosts oil. Gilts (UK government bonds) are actually rallying slightly — the 10-year yield fell 6 basis points (a basis point is one-hundredth of a percent), and long-end stress is absent, so there is no fiscal alarm to worry about. The net result is a tug-of-war: energy is pulling up, US tech weakness and risk-off sentiment are pulling down, leaving the index essentially flat on the day (-0.29%). Directional bias leans mildly BEARISH-to-CHOPPY from here — the US selloff and European weakness are hard to ignore, but the energy cushion prevents a clean breakdown. Confidence is 4/10; the main thing that would change this view is a surprise reversal in US futures overnight or a further escalation (or de-escalation) in US-Iran headlines. For the 08:00 ORB trade tomorrow, today's macro backdrop suggests a fakeout/sweep-then-reverse day is more likely than a clean trend day — the opposing forces (oil bull vs US bear) create whipsaw conditions where false breakouts are common. On event risk: US CPI (inflation data — market-moving for rates globally) is due tomorrow at 13:30 BST, which is a HIGH-impact event arriving after the ORB window; still, it may cause pre-release position-squaring that muddies the morning. UK GDP is due Wednesday 07:00 BST — a rare pre-open release that could gap the index. On key levels: the overnight range ran from 10,443 to 10,526 (a span of 83 points); the ORB already broke DOWN through its low of 10,482, with the ORB high at 10,526 acting as resistance; the 14-day average daily range is 133 points and 62% of it has already been used, so there is roughly 50 points of "range budget" left — don't chase a big move from open. Watch 10,443 (overnight low / support) below and 10,526–10,537 (overnight high / prior day high) as resistance above. Remember: energy is the bull, the US tape is the bear — whoever wins that fight at 08:00 sets the ORB direction.
